candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance → Health Promotion/Disease Prevention: identify client risk factors, provide preventive education, support healthy lifestyle behaviors, and promote management of chronic risk conditions before complications develop.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — primary prevention of heart failure through modifiable risk-factor management
candidate.educational_objective: Reduce future heart-failure risk by identifying and addressing modifiable Stage A risk factors before symptomatic or structural heart failure develops.

options.A: Work with the health care team to control blood pressure and diabetes, address excess weight, remain physically active, follow a heart-healthy eating pattern, and avoid smoking.
options.B: Heart-failure prevention is determined mainly by inherited factors, so controlling blood pressure, weight, glucose, and smoking has little preventive value.
options.C: Risk-factor management becomes useful only after symptoms or structural heart disease have already developed.
options.D: Because the client does not yet have heart failure, cardiovascular risk-factor treatment is unrelated to future heart-failure prevention.

candidate.rationale: Current American Heart Association primary-prevention guidance identifies hypertension, diabetes, obesity, chronic kidney disease, and coronary artery disease among important modifiable or treatable contributors to heart-failure risk and emphasizes lifestyle measures such as healthy diet, physical activity, weight management, and tobacco avoidance. The AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline similarly classifies people with hypertension, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, diabetes, metabolic syndrome, or obesity as Stage A—at risk for heart failure—and recommends risk-factor modification before symptomatic disease develops. Therefore, A is correct. B, C, and D incorrectly minimize primary prevention.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports active management of hypertension, diabetes, obesity and other cardiovascular risk factors plus healthy lifestyle behaviors to reduce heart-failure risk before clinical HF develops.
candidate.source_document_title: Risk-Based Primary Prevention of Heart Failure: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association; 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
candidate.source_locator: AHA 2025 'Risk-Based Primary Prevention of Heart Failure' → Top Things to Know items 2 and 8: prevention integrates lifestyle intervention and management of hypertension, diabetes, obesity, CKD, and CAD using pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic approaches. 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline → Section 2.1 Table 3 Stage A and Section 5.1: Stage A includes hypertension, atherosclerotic CVD, diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity; healthy physical activity, normal weight/BP/glucose, healthy dietary patterns and not smoking are associated with lower lifetime HF risk.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association; American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
candidate.source_version_date: AHA scientific statement updated 2025-04-16; HF guideline 2022-04-01
candidate.stem: A nurse is counseling an adult who does not have heart failure but has hypertension, obesity, and type 2 diabetes. Which teaching best addresses modifiable heart-failure risk?
